title: Segmenting a French Meeting Corpus into Elementary Discourse Units
research_question: Can a manually annotated French meeting corpus support reliable elementary discourse unit segmentation with a fine-tuned language model and limited annotation effort?
methodology: The authors annotate SUMM-RE meeting transcripts speaker by speaker in Praat, using training and guideline discussions followed by manual-seed pre-segmentation and human editing (U02-S03–S06). They fine-tune xlm-roberta-large through the cited JIANT/DisCut methodology, described in the paper as sequence-to-sequence, while operationalizing the output as a binary EDU-start label per token in CoNLL/DISRPT format (U02-S07, S12). They vary the number of gold training tokens and report positive-boundary precision, recall, and F-score (U02-S11). Training hyperparameters and all exact scores are in topic02.metrics; the downstream split allocation is not reported. Prosody is not evaluated (U02-S14).

key_findings.finding: The annotated representation is a single layer of contiguous-token EDUs, each expressing a semantic proposition or one speech act, with preparatory disfluencies retained inside the unit.
key_findings.quote: span of contiguous tokens whose combined meaning corresponds to a semantic proposi- tion (describing an event, fact, or state of af- fairs), or a single speech act, such as asking a question, providing an answer, or offering conversational feedback. All preparatory disfluent material should be included within the unit.

key_findings.finding: Segmentation is independent for each speaker with full conversational context available; abandoned false starts become separate units, while coherent preparatory hesitations remain with the following content.
key_findings.quote: It is important to note that segmentation is performed independently for each participant, although annotators are allowed to see the full multilogue context.

key_findings.finding: Section 4 reports manual correction and annotation of the original SUMM-RE dev/test portions: 73 meetings and approximately 24 hours; the abstract and conclusion instead describe 20 hours of manual data.
key_findings.quote: The full dev and test sets— corresponding to 73 meetings and approximately 24 hours of recordings—have been manually corrected and annotated.

key_findings.finding: A small manual seed trained a rough pre-segmenter, after which annotators edited its output; the authors report sample inspection and no significant difference in agreement between from-scratch and pre-segmented files, while explicitly retaining possible bias.
key_findings.quote: Second, we performed inter-coder agreement analysis on both files annotated from scratch and those annotated with pre-segmentation, and ob- served no significant differences between the two.

key_findings.finding: The prose reports semi-naive annotator mean κ of 0.85–0.89 and expert κ around 0.9, whereas Figure 1 explicitly presents human F-scores and Figure 2 labels its red reference only as the human-annotation mean; these quantities cannot be treated as a verified common metric.
key_findings.section: PDF p. 4, Section 5.1; compare Figure 1 and PDF p. 5 Figure 2
key_findings.quote: Overall, semi-naive coder reached mean κ-scores within the 0.85-0.89 range, while a few expert annotations conduced by the authors of the paper have shown higher reliability, with κ-scores around 0.9.

key_findings.finding: For SUMM-RE gold-data EDU-boundary prediction, Table 1 reports precision 0.900, recall 0.831, and F-score 0.864 with 100,000 training tokens; gains flatten across the larger reported training sizes, but the exact evaluation partition and boundary counts are not supplied.
key_findings.section: PDF p. 8, Appendix, Table 1; evaluation definition in PDF pp. 4–5 Section 6
key_findings.quote: 100000 0.900 0.831 0.864 Table 1: Results for Discourse Segmentation for different amount of training gold data.

key_findings.finding: The authors suggest that the observed model plateau corresponds to a maximal theoretical performance level because it aligns with inter-coder agreement.
key_findings.evidence_basis: author interpretation; no theoretical bound, common-metric validation, repeated-run uncertainty, or expert-gold ceiling experiment
key_findings.quote: Notably, this performance plateau seems to correspond to the maximal theoretical level achievable, as it aligns with the inter-coder agreement levels observed in our study.

key_findings.finding: The paper describes automatically transcribed and segmented output, but leaves assessment of segmentation on ASR versions to future work; no ASR segmentation evaluation is established by the reported output volume.
key_findings.evidence_basis: explicit future-work statement and full-paper evaluation-scope audit; no negative ASR result implied
key_findings.section: PDF p. 5, Section 7: ASR future work
key_findings.quote: For future work, we are interested in assessing the extent to which discourse segmentation can be effectively applied to the ASR versions of the corpus.

key_findings.finding: Appendix examples place a reason introduced by puisque and a corrective restriction introduced by mais in separate EDUs; they illustrate segmentation conventions without measuring retention of the relation to the preceding content.
key_findings.evidence_basis: visible annotation examples, not a scope-preservation experiment

limitations: French event-planning meeting speech provides qualified transfer to business email; no email or asynchronous Topic evaluation appears (U02-S02, S07, S11).
Contiguous EDUs and binary start labels provide no gold or predicted Topic membership, overlapping semantic assignments, or discontinuous Topic objects (U02-F01; U02-S12).

No comparative preservation evaluation selects an EDU over a sentence, clause, arbitrary span, or hybrid; conditions, evidence links, exceptions, action scope, approval scope, and reply scope are not scored (U02-S06, S07, S10, S11).

Original corpus dev/test annotation coverage does not identify downstream training, development, and evaluation membership; meeting/group/speaker isolation, duplicate controls, seeds, and repeated-run statistics are not reported (U02-S02, S04, S07, S11).
Pre-segmentation checks lack sample sizes, test identity, p-values, effect sizes, or a fully independent gold comparison; the paper itself does not exclude annotation bias (U02-F04).
Human κ prose, human F-score plots, corpus-duration statements, participant coverage, and table references require the qualifications in material_inconsistencies (U02-F03, F05).

Boundary F-score does not establish exact whole-EDU span accuracy, semantic relation preservation, or a theoretical ceiling; no detailed boundary-error taxonomy or preservation-error count is provided (U02-F06, F07, F09).

ASR applicability, expert-annotation improvement, and the discourse-prosody interface are future directions, not evaluated results here; laughter is excluded from the segmentation work (U02-F08; U02-S03, S09, S14).

confidence_score_semantics: Confidence in evidential support for the stated finding, not a reproduced result; the unsupported theoretical-ceiling claim receives low confidence even though its attribution is certain.
raw_claims: Regarding major dialogic phenomena, whenever a backchannel corresponds to a full dialogue act, it is segmented accordingly.
A unit is only labeled as an abandoned discourse unit if the introduced material is discarded before the beginning of a different discourse unit.
Our guidelines use both holistic interpretation of discourse function within the discourse flow as understood by the annotator and surface cues such as discourse markers.
The results in Figure 2 indicate that the model’s performance plateaus relatively quickly.
The model, along with its application to the full dataset, will be released alongside the code repository.

annotation_unit.unit: Contiguous tokens constituting a proposition/event/fact/state or one speech act, with preparatory disfluencies; one layer per speaker.
annotation_unit.context: Other speakers remain visible to the annotator; boundaries are timed in separate Praat files.

prediction_unit.unit: One binary EDU-start decision per token; Table 2 illustrates BeginSeg=Yes versus underscore.
prediction_unit.labels_are_not: Topic identities or semantic speech-act classes.

contiguity.gold: EDUs explicitly contain contiguous tokens in the speaker transcript.
contiguity.prediction: Binary starts induce sequential contiguous units in the input sequence; there is no non-sequential cluster output.

gold.boundary: One of two boundary states per token in the segmentation encoding; one EDU layer per speaker. The guidelines also discuss abandoned units, but no separate abandoned-unit classification results are reported.
gold.topic: No Topic labels or Topic-membership cardinalities are annotated or evaluated.

prediction.boundary: One binary start/non-start state per token.
prediction.topic: No model output for Topic membership or multi-label cardinality.

gold.one_semantic_object: Each EDU is contiguous; no disconnected spans assigned to the same Topic or EDU object.
gold.within_one_message: Email/message-local discontinuous assignment is not represented or evaluated.
gold.thread_level: No Topic cluster links across messages or nonadjacent speaker contributions; no thread-level discontinuity evaluation.

prediction.one_semantic_object: Binary starts provide no discontinuous-object identity.

gold.semantic_token_membership: The single-layer segmentation does not represent overlapping semantic spans or multiple Topic memberships.
gold.temporal_speaker_overlap: Independent timed speaker files can coexist during simultaneous speech; this is an analyst inference about the annotation format, not semantic token overlap or a reported overlap-rate measurement.

prediction.semantic_token_membership: Unsupported by the binary start representation; not evaluated.
prediction.temporal_speaker_overlap: No separate overlap-detection model or metric is reported.

overlap.within_message_vs_thread: Neither within-message Topic span overlap nor thread-level multi-membership is evaluated.

metrics.task: EDU-start boundary detection on SUMM-RE manually annotated conversational French data.
metrics.paper_definition: Precision, recall, and F-score computed exclusively for discourse boundaries, excluding true negatives.
metrics.denominator_interpretation: For positive-boundary scoring, precision uses predicted starts and recall uses gold starts; F1 is their harmonic mean. These are standard metric interpretations, not explicit equations printed by this paper.
metrics.unknown_denominators: Gold and predicted boundary counts, token count of evaluation data, first-token treatment, aggregation level, and error tolerance are not specified.

RQ1.assessment: Useful EDU operational definition and annotation examples; no comparative evidence establishes the best unit for a work matter.

RQ2.assessment: No direct email/asynchronous clustering or interleaving evidence; speaker-local segmentation is not Topic linking.

RQ3.assessment: Makes the absence of gold/predicted multi-Topic membership clear; binary boundaries do not solve Topic cardinality.

RQ4.assessment: Single contiguous layer supplies no overlapping/discontinuous Topic representation; timed speaker overlap is a different property.

RQ5.assessment: Disfluency-retention rules and reason/correction examples suggest risks to test; no measured scope-preservation outcome.

RQ6.assessment: Useful positive-boundary precision/recall/F-score evidence with missing denominators and ambiguous human metric comparison.

RQ7.assessment: Relevant annotation protocol, domain limits, and bias check; unresolved size statements and missing downstream splits limit reproducibility.

RQ8.assessment: Motivates controlled unit, preservation, and annotation-bias experiments only; no architecture approval.

interpretation.label: analyst interpretation
interpretation.text: An EDU can be a candidate evidence unit, but its single-proposition or speech-act definition does not establish a concrete work matter’s full scope. Grouping EDUs requires a separate evaluated Topic assignment.

interpretation.label: analyst interpretation
interpretation.text: A segmentation that isolates a reason or corrective restriction can remain linguistically valid. Later selecting only one unit could omit decision-bearing context; that is a plausible downstream risk, not a measured paper error.

interpretation.label: analyst interpretation
interpretation.text: The learning curve suggests a possible pilot annotation budget for this EDU task, but neither its asymptote nor human agreement supplies a guaranteed performance ceiling, email score, or safe preservation threshold.

interpretation.label: analyst interpretation
interpretation.text: Separate timed speaker files permit temporal concurrency without giving one text span multiple semantic memberships; no thread-level or within-message Topic discontinuity follows.
